question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z\ge -2.06).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.1\,$ | $\,0.0162\,$ | $\,0.0158\,$ | $\,0.0154\,$ |
| $\,-2.0\,$ | $\,0.0207\,$ | $\,0.0202\,$ | $\,0.0197\,$ |
| $\,-1.9\,$ | $\,0.0262\,$ | $\,0.0256\,$ | $\,0.0250\,$ |

$P(Z\ge -2.06)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge -2.06).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/30c8380c76e236d13780e3fd6f9dc2b5a76f825ac55411befc3d7fddf07c452d.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -2.06) & =1-P(Z<-2.06) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.06).\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/6a1cfc6c71b551cdde6880007fc1eee1cb439a0e32443a406dee0fdac3f112e4.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-2.06)=0.0197.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -2.06) & =1-Φ(-2.06) \\  & =1-0.0197 \\  & =0.9803.\end{aligned}
$$
